name: Garage Dreams
description: From Apple's garage to Facebook's dorm room: the chips, machines and companies that started small and built the personal computer and internet industries.

checkpoints.name: Kits and garages
checkpoints.note: Intel's 4004 and 8080 and the cheap MOS 6502 put a computer's brain on a chip, and at Xerox PARC the Alto showed a mouse and windows. Hobbyists built the Altair from a kit, Bill Gates left Harvard to start Microsoft, and in 1976 Steve Wozniak and Steve Jobs built the Apple I and founded Apple, whose Apple II of 1977 came ready to use.

checkpoints.name: The beige box
checkpoints.note: IBM enters with the IBM PC and Microsoft's MS-DOS, and the deal makes the small company that began in Albuquerque the most important name in software. Apple answers with the Lisa, built on ideas Jobs had seen at Xerox PARC.

checkpoints.name: Mouse and windows
checkpoints.note: The Macintosh brings the mouse and windows to ordinary buyers in 1984, and Jobs is pushed out of Apple a year later. The PC and the Mac settle in as the two main camps, and in 1994 two Stanford students turn a list of websites into Yahoo.

checkpoints.name: Everyone online
checkpoints.note: Jeff Bezos starts Amazon in his garage, two Stanford students build Google Search and rent their first office in a garage, and Jobs returns to Apple, where the iMac revives the company. In 2004 Mark Zuckerberg launches Facebook from his Harvard dorm room.
